Current Grade: 7.5/10 — These improvements target 9/10+ by fixing critical security issues, adding automated testing infrastructure, improving accessibility, and strengthening the code generation pipeline.

🚨 Phase 1 — Critical Fixes (Week 1)

Highest impact, lowest effort. These are the must-fix items before anything else.

1.1 Fix XSS in App Generation Pipeline Quick fix

CRITICAL Problem: 3 generated apps (expense-tracker, chat-app, kanban-board) use innerHTML with unsanitized user input. The CodeScanner.ts already detects this pattern but doesn't prevent it during generation.

Fix: Add HTML entity escaping as a post-generation step in the scaffolder:

// Add this utility to scaffolder.ts
function escapeHtml(str) {
  return str.replace(/&/g, '&')
            .replace(//g, '>')
            .replace(/"/g, '"')
            .replace(/'/g, ''');
}

// Auto-fix innerHTML assignments with escaped content

Bonus: The previewHtmlBuilder.ts already has an escapeHtml() function — reuse it in the scaffolder for generated app output.

1.2 Automatic Post-Gen Security Scan Quick fix

CRITICAL Problem: The CodeScanner.securityScan() method already exists and detects XSS, eval(), SQL injection, and 12 other vulnerability types — but it's not automatically called after code generation.

Fix: Add a postGenerationScan step in the generation pipeline that:

  1. Runs securityScan() on every generated file
  2. Blocks deployment if critical/high vulnerabilities found
  3. Returns scan report to the user with remediation suggestions

Impact: Zero new code needed — just wire up the existing scanner into the generation pipeline.

1.3 Replace eval() in Sandbox with Safe Runner Medium effort

CRITICAL Problem: The sandbox preview uses eval(appCode) to run generated JavaScript. This is a security risk — generated code could access the parent window's DOM, localStorage, or cookies.

Fix: Replace eval() with an iframe-based sandbox:

// Instead of: eval(appCode);
// Use:
const iframe = document.createElement('iframe');
iframe.sandbox = 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin';
iframe.srcdoc = `<script>${appCode}</script>`;
iframe.style.display = 'none';
document.body.appendChild(iframe);

Impact: Prevents sandbox code from accessing the parent application entirely.

⚡ Phase 2 — Core Architecture (Week 2-3)

Medium effort, high impact. These improve reliability, accuracy, and user experience.

2.1 App Testing Automation Medium effort

HIGH Problem: Apps were tested manually via browser — no automated test harness exists. This makes regression testing impossible.

Fix: Create an automated app test suite that:

  1. Launches each HTML app in a headless browser (Puppeteer/Playwright)
  2. Checks for: page load, console errors, interactive elements, keyboard nav
  3. Generates a test report with pass/fail for each app
  4. Runs on every code generation to catch regressions

Suggested tool: Vitest + Playwright (already have Vitest in deps)

// Instead of:
setInterval(() => { timeLeft--; }, 1000);

// Use:
const startTime = Date.now();

  const remaining = Math.max(0, duration - elapsed);
  updateDisplay(Math.ceil(remaining / 1000));

}, 100); // check every 100ms for accuracy

instruction: Fix the 3D solar system app (THREE.OrbitPath crash)
input: The app crashed with 'THREE.OrbitPath is not a constructor'. OrbitPath is not a real Three.js class. Fix it: load OrbitControls from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js, create controls with new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement), draw orbit rings with THREE.Line + BufferGeometry.setFromPoints of cos/sin points, store each planet's {distance, speed, angle} in userData, and advance angle in the animate loop.
output:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
	<meta charset="UTF-8">
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
	<title>3D Solar System</title>
	<style>
		body { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; background: #000; }
		#canvas { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
	</style>
</head>
<body>
	<canvas id="canvas"></canvas>
	<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js"></script>
	<script>
		const scene = new THREE.Scene();
		const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
		const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true });
		renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
		document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
		camera.position.set(0, 0, 100);
		const controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement);
		controls.enableDamping = true;
		controls.dampingFactor = 0.05;
		scene.add(new THREE.AxesHelper(10));
		const planets = [];
		function addPlanet(name, color, radius, distance, speed) {
			const geometry = new THREE.SphereGeometry(radius, 32, 32);
			const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color, flatShading: true });
			const planet = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
			const orbit = new THREE.Line(
				new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(
					Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, i) => {
						const a = (i / 64) * Math.PI * 2;
						return new THREE.Vector3(Math.cos(a) * distance, 0, Math.sin(a) * distance);
					})),
				new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0x334466, transparent: true, opacity: 0.5 })
			);
			scene.add(orbit);
			planet.userData = { distance, speed, angle: Math.random() * Math.PI * 2 };
			planet.position.x = distance * Math.cos(planet.userData.angle);
			planet.position.y = 0;
			planet.position.z = distance * Math.sin(planet.userData.angle);
			scene.add(planet);
			planets.push(planet);
			return planet;
		}
		const sun = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(5, 32, 32), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xffffd5, emissive: 0xaaaaaa, roughness: 0.2, metalness: 0.8 }));
		sun.castShadow = true;
		scene.add(sun);
		const saturn = addPlanet('Saturn', 0x0080ff, 1, 15, 0.01);
		const rings = [];
		for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
			const ring = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.TorusGeometry(5, 0.5, 32, 32), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x80ff80, flatShading: true }));
			ring.position.x = 14.5;
			ring.position.z = 0.5 * (2 * i - 1);
			rings.push(ring);
			scene.add(ring);
		}
		function animate() {
			requestAnimationFrame(animate);
			sun.rotation.y += 0.005;
			planets.forEach(p => {
				p.userData.angle += 0.002 * p.userData.speed;
				p.position.x = p.userData.distance * Math.cos(p.userData.angle);
				p.position.z = p.userData.distance * Math.sin(p.userData.angle);
			});
			controls.update();
			renderer.render(scene, camera);
		}
		animate();
	</script>
</body>
</html>

instruction: Build a 3D Rook chess piece
input:
Single-file HTML, Three.js r128 via CDN (global THREE + OrbitControls). A SINGLE detailed 3D rook chess piece STANDING UPRIGHT in the middle of the scene. COMPOSITION RULES — follow them exactly:
1. STACK the parts along the Y axis with explicit, non-overlapping y positions: base plinth (a flattened cylinder, e.g. radius 1.1, height 0.25) centered at y=-1.5 (spans -1.625..-1.375), tapered shaft (CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height) — radiusTop is FIRST, so a shaft narrow at top is CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.9, 1.4, 32)) centered at y=-0.6 (spans -1.3..0.1, seated on the plinth), a flared collar (radius 0.6, height 0.1) centered at y=0.3, and the crenellated top (radius 0.45, height 0.3) centered at y=0.6 (spans 0.45..0.75). REMEMBER: position.y is the CENTER of a part, NOT its bottom — compute it as (partTop + partBottom) / 2 so parts just touch.
2. The piece must STAND VERTICAL — do NOT rotate the group (no rotation.x set; keep the Y axis as the piece's long axis).
3. Battlements: exactly 5 small cylinders (radius 0.12, height 0.25) arranged in a RING around the top rim at a fixed radius (0.45) and fixed angles (i * 2*PI/5 for i in 0..4) — use a loop with trig, NEVER Math.random() for placement.
4. FRAMING: camera.position.set(3, 2.2, 5), camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0), controls.target.set(0, 0, 0) so the whole piece fills the middle of the frame.
5. LIGHTING — critical: a metal material (metalness >0.8) reflects almost NO diffuse, so a single weak light makes it render NEARLY BLACK. Use metalness 0.6-0.75, roughness ~0.3, a strong key light (PointLight intensity >= 2.5) PLUS a directional fill light from the opposite side PLUS an ambient >= 0x444444. Soft shadows, warm spotlight from the upper right, gentle slow auto-rotation of the piece, OrbitControls.
6. NAMING: never declare a top-level const named `top`, `name`, `length`, or `status` (built-in globals) — use descriptive names like `crownTop`.
7. No textures, no external assets. Two-script rule: when using THREE.OrbitControls you MUST load BOTH https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js before the app script.
output:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>3D Rook Chess Piece</title>
  <style>
    html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: #111; }
    #scene { position: fixed; inset: 0; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <canvas id="scene"></canvas>
  <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js"></script>
  <script>
    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas: document.querySelector('#scene') });
    renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
    const controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement);
    camera.position.set(2.6, 2.0, 4.2);
    camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0);
    controls.target.set(0, 0, 0);
    scene.background = new THREE.Color(0x4a4a4a);
    scene.fog = new THREE.Fog(0x4a4a4a, 20, 100);
    const ambient = new THREE.AmbientLight(0x444444);
    scene.add(ambient);
    const light = new THREE.PointLight(0xffffff, 2.5);
    light.position.set(5, 5, 5);
    scene.add(light);
    const fill = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.2);
    fill.position.set(-4, 3, -3);
    scene.add(fill);
    const rook = new THREE.Group();
    const base = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(1.1, 1.1, 0.25, 32);
    const baseMesh = new THREE.Mesh(base, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    baseMesh.position.y = -1.5;
    rook.add(baseMesh);
    const shaft = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.9, 1.4, 32);
    const shaftMesh = new THREE.Mesh(shaft, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    shaftMesh.position.y = -0.6;
    rook.add(shaftMesh);
    const collar = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.6, 0.6, 0.1, 32);
    const collarMesh = new THREE.Mesh(collar, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    collarMesh.position.y = 0.3;
    rook.add(collarMesh);
    const crown = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.45, 0.45, 0.3, 32);
    const topMesh = new THREE.Mesh(crown, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    topMesh.position.y = 0.5;
    const battlements = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      const battlement = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.12, 0.12, 0.25, 32);
      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(battlement, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
      mesh.position.set(0.45 * Math.cos(i * 2 * Math.PI / 5), 0.28, 0.45 * Math.sin(i * 2 * Math.PI / 5));
      mesh.rotation.x = 0;
      battlements.push(mesh);
      topMesh.add(mesh);
    }
    topMesh.position.y = 0.6;
    rook.add(topMesh);
    scene.add(rook);
    const clock = new THREE.Clock();
    function animate() {
      const t = clock.getElapsedTime();
      rook.rotation.y = t * 0.1;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
      requestAnimationFrame(animate);
    }
    animate();
    window.addEventListener('resize', () => {
      camera.aspect = window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>

instruction: QA rule: a game app must be a game — rendering a scene is not enough
input: A 3D chess app renders a beautiful board and pieces with zero console errors, but clicking does nothing, there is no move function, no captures and no check detection, and the board spins by itself. Why is it still broken, and what must a chess app have?
output:
Rendering is the surface; the game is the logic. A chess app is only done when it actually plays:
  1. TWO sides of pieces (black AND white, 16 each, with correct colors)
  2. a click handler (Raycaster pick -> select a piece -> show legal moves -> click a destination to move)
  3. a move() that updates a real 8x8 board state, animates the piece, and handles captures (removing the victim)
  4. turn alternation, legal-move filtering, and check/checkmate detection
  5. a static board (the camera orbits, the board does not spin)
Verify by PLAYING the app, not just by watching it render.

instruction: Fix the 3D chess app (broken texture URLs)
input: The app 404'd on threejs.org/examples/textures/chess1.png, chess2.png, wood.jpg. Never depend on external image assets. Fix it: generate the checkerboard with a canvas + CanvasTexture (fill 8x8 alternating squares), and give pieces solid MeshStandardMaterial colors instead of image textures.
output:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<meta charset="UTF-8">
	<title>3D Chess Game</title>
	<style>
		body { margin: 0; }
		canvas { width: 100%; height: 100%; display: block; }
	</style>
</head>
<body>
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js"></script>

<script>
	
	var scene = new THREE.Scene();
	scene.background = new THREE.Color('grey');
	
	var camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(45, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
	camera.position.set(0, 0, 10);
	
	var renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer();
	renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
	document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
	
	var controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement);
	controls.enableDamping = true;
	controls.dampingFactor = 0.05;
	
	var light = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 0.5);
	light.position.set(1, 1, 1).normalize();
	scene.add(light);
	
	function makeCheckerTexture() {
		var c = document.createElement('canvas');
		c.width = c.height = 256;
		var ctx = c.getContext('2d');
		var s = 32;
		for (var x = 0; x < 8; x++) {
			for (var y = 0; y < 8; y++) {
				ctx.fillStyle = (x + y) % 2 ? '#3a2414' : '#e8d3a3';
				ctx.fillRect(x * s, y * s, s, s);
			}
		}
		return new THREE.CanvasTexture(c);
	}
	var boardTexture = makeCheckerTexture();
	var boardGeometry = new THREE.BoxGeometry(8, 8, 0.1);
	var boardMaterial = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ map: boardTexture, side: THREE.DoubleSide });
	var board = new THREE.Mesh(boardGeometry, boardMaterial);
	scene.add(board);
	
	var pieceGeometries = [];
	var pieceMaterials = [];
	for (var i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
		var geometry = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 0.1);
		var material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: i % 2 ? 0xdddddd : 0x333333, roughness: 0.5 });
		pieceGeometries.push(geometry);
		pieceMaterials.push(material);
	}
	var pieces = [];
	for (var i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
		var mesh = new THREE.Mesh(pieceGeometries[i], pieceMaterials[i]);
		pieces.push(mesh);
		scene.add(mesh);
	}
	
	var selectedPiece = null;
	var selectedSquare = null;
	var movePiece = function(mesh, square) {
		
		mesh.position.set(square.x * 1.5, square.y * 1.5, -0.5);
		
		selectedPiece = null;
		selectedSquare = null;
	};
	var highlightSquare = function(square) {
		
		var highlightGeometry = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.5, 1.5, 0.1);
		var highlightMaterial = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xff0000, side: THREE.DoubleSide });
		var highlightMesh = new THREE.Mesh(highlightGeometry, highlightMaterial);
		highlightMesh.position.set(square.x * 1.5, square.y * 1.5, -0.5);
		scene.add(highlightMesh);
		
		var children = scene.children.filter(function(child) { return child.name === 'highlight'; });
		for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
			scene.remove(children[i]);
		}
	};
	
	var turn = 0;
	var turnIndicator = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1), new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xffffff, side: THREE.DoubleSide }));
	turnIndicator.position.set(9 * 1.5, 0, -0.5);
	turnIndicator.name = 'turnIndicator';
	scene.add(turnIndicator);
	
	var render = function() {
		requestAnimationFrame(render);
		
		if (selectedPiece) {
			var square = selectedSquare;
			var piece = selectedPiece;
			
			if (turn % 2 === 0) {
				
				
			} else {
				
				
			}
			
			movePiece(piece, square);
			
			highlightSquare(square);
		}
		
		controls.update();
		
		renderer.render(scene, camera);
	};
	
	render();
</script>
</body>
</html>

instruction: QA rule: the CDN URL is case-sensitive — always three.min.js (lowercase)

https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js

instruction: Instance hundreds of buildings with InstancedMesh
input: Three.js r128. instruction: QA rule: only use THREE classes that exist in r128 — never invent APIs
input: An app did const colorGradient = new THREE.ColorGradient(); and the whole script died with 'THREE.ColorGradient is not a constructor'. Is that a real class?
output: No. THREE.ColorGradient does not exist in r128. Never call new THREE.<Anything>() unless you are sure it ships in three.min.js r128. Use real classes instead: THREE.Color for colors (with .setHSL / .lerpColors for gradients) or THREE.BufferAttribute / vertex colors. When unsure, check the three.js docs for r128; a constructor that does not exist throws at the line where it is called and kills the entire script.

instruction: QA rule: never name a top-level const after a built-in global (top, name, length, status)
input: An app's whole script failed with 'Identifier top has already been declared' even though the code looked fine. THREE loaded, but nothing ran. Why?
output: window.top, window.name, window.length, window.status and similar are EXISTING built-in globals. A top-level `const top = ...` in a classic script collides with them and throws 'Identifier ... has already been declared' at script instantiation — the ENTIRE script never runs (every other const stays in TDZ). Use descriptive names instead: `const crownTop`, `const pieceName`, `const listLength` — never the bare reserved word.

🔧 System Improvement Blueprint

Based on analysis of 24 apps • 7.5/10 current grade • Target: 9/10+

Current Grade: 7.5/10 — These improvements target 9/10+ by fixing critical security issues, adding automated testing infrastructure, improving accessibility, and strengthening the code generation pipeline.

🚨 Phase 1 — Critical Fixes (Week 1)

Highest impact, lowest effort. These are the must-fix items before anything else.

1.1 Fix XSS in App Generation Pipeline Quick fix

CRITICAL Problem: 3 generated apps (expense-tracker, chat-app, kanban-board) use innerHTML with unsanitized user input. The CodeScanner.ts already detects this pattern but doesn't prevent it during generation.

Fix: Add HTML entity escaping as a post-generation step in the scaffolder:

// Add this utility to scaffolder.ts
function escapeHtml(str) {
  return str.replace(/&/g, '&')
            .replace(//g, '>')
            .replace(/"/g, '"')
            .replace(/'/g, ''');
}

// Run securityScan on generated HTML before writing
// Auto-fix innerHTML assignments with escaped content

Bonus: The previewHtmlBuilder.ts already has an escapeHtml() function — reuse it in the scaffolder for generated app output.

1.2 Automatic Post-Gen Security Scan Quick fix

CRITICAL Problem: The CodeScanner.securityScan() method already exists and detects XSS, eval(), SQL injection, and 12 other vulnerability types — but it's not automatically called after code generation.

Fix: Add a postGenerationScan step in the generation pipeline that:

  1. Runs securityScan() on every generated file
  2. Blocks deployment if critical/high vulnerabilities found
  3. Returns scan report to the user with remediation suggestions

Impact: Zero new code needed — just wire up the existing scanner into the generation pipeline.

1.3 Replace eval() in Sandbox with Safe Runner Medium effort

CRITICAL Problem: The sandbox preview uses eval(appCode) to run generated JavaScript. This is a security risk — generated code could access the parent window's DOM, localStorage, or cookies.

Fix: Replace eval() with an iframe-based sandbox:

// Instead of: eval(appCode);
// Use:
const iframe = document.createElement('iframe');
iframe.sandbox = 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin';
iframe.srcdoc = `<script>${appCode}</script>`;
iframe.style.display = 'none';
document.body.appendChild(iframe);

Impact: Prevents sandbox code from accessing the parent application entirely.

⚡ Phase 2 — Core Architecture (Week 2-3)

Medium effort, high impact. These improve reliability, accuracy, and user experience.

2.1 App Testing Automation Medium effort

HIGH Problem: Apps were tested manually via browser — no automated test harness exists. This makes regression testing impossible.

Fix: Create an automated app test suite that:

  1. Launches each HTML app in a headless browser (Puppeteer/Playwright)
  2. Checks for: page load, console errors, interactive elements, keyboard nav
  3. Generates a test report with pass/fail for each app
  4. Runs on every code generation to catch regressions

Suggested tool: Vitest + Playwright (already have Vitest in deps)

2.2 Timer Accuracy Fix Quick fix

HIGH Problem: Multiple apps use setInterval(fn, 1000) which drifts over time. The pomodoro timer could be off by 3-5 seconds after 25 minutes.

Fix: Replace with Date.now() differential pattern:

// Instead of:
setInterval(() => { timeLeft--; }, 1000);

// Use:
const startTime = Date.now();
const duration = 25 * 60 * 1000;
setInterval(() => {
  const elapsed = Date.now() - startTime;
  const remaining = Math.max(0, duration - elapsed);
  updateDisplay(Math.ceil(remaining / 1000));
  if (remaining <= 0) onComplete();
}, 100); // check every 100ms for accuracy

Apps affected: pomodoro-timer, music-player, typing-test

2.3 Add Accessibility Scaffold to Generated Apps Medium effort

HIGH Problem: All 24 apps lack ARIA labels, proper heading hierarchy, and keyboard navigation support.

Fix: Create an accessibility plugin for the scaffolder that automatically adds:

  • lang="en" attribute to all HTML documents
  • role="button" and aria-label on interactive elements
  • tabindex and keyboard event handlers
  • Focus management for modals and dynamic content
  • Color contrast verification (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance)

2.4 Mobile Touch Support for Kanban Medium effort

MEDIUM Problem: HTML5 Drag and Drop API doesn't work on touch devices. The kanban board is unusable on mobile.

Fix: Add touch event handlers (touchstart, touchmove, touchend) that mirror the drag/drop behavior. Use elementFromPoint() to detect drop targets on touch devices.

🚀 Phase 3 — Advanced Features (Week 4-6)

Larger efforts that unlock major capability improvements.

3.1 Multi-Framework App Generation Templates Big effort

MEDIUM Problem: Currently all apps are vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. No React, Vue, Svelte, or Next.js support.

Fix: Extend the scaffolder with template engines:

  • React: Generate JSX components with Vite build config
  • Vue: Generate SFC (.vue) files with Vite
  • Svelte: Generate .svelte files
  • Next.js: Generate pages/api structure

Piggyback on existing system: The node types and data flow already exist — just swap the output template.

3.2 Interactive Live Preview Big effort

MEDIUM Problem: The sandbox preview is a static HTML page. Users can't see changes as they edit nodes.

Fix: Implement WebSocket-based live preview that:

  1. Streams code changes in real-time as nodes are edited
  2. Hot-reloads the preview without full page refresh
  3. Shows compilation errors inline in the node editor

Architecture: The socket.io-client is already in package.json — just need a Socket.IO server for streaming code changes.

3.3 AI-Powered Fix Suggestions Big effort

MEDIUM Problem: When code generation produces errors, the user sees raw error messages with no guidance on how to fix them.

Fix: Pipe CodeScanner results + error output into the LLM to generate human-readable fix suggestions:

1. Run generated code → catch errors
2. Run CodeScanner → get vulnerability report
3. Send both to LLM: "Here's the code, here's the error,
   here are security issues found. Suggest fixes."
4. Display fix suggestions with diff view

3.4 Backend Reliability & Offline Mode Big effort

CRITICAL Problem: Backend went down multiple times during testing. No offline fallback — entire app breaks when backend is unavailable.

Fix: Multi-pronged approach:

  • Retry with exponential backoff: All API calls retry 3× with 1s/2s/4s delays
  • Offline queue: Queue failed operations and replay when backend recovers
  • Local-only mode: Detect backend status and fall back to localStorage for all operations
  • Health endpoint: Add /api/health with DB connection check, disk space, uptime

instruction: QA rule: a GUI app must have working JavaScript — not just styled HTML
input: An app for a weather dashboard passed visual inspection but had zero <script> tags: no search, no unit toggle, no data updates. Why is that a failure, and what must a GUI app contain?
output: A GUI app's job is INTERACTION. HTML+CSS alone is a static mockup. A complete app needs: (1) a <script> block with the state and logic, (2) event wiring — button.onclick / addEventListener for every control, (3) a render path that updates the DOM from state (render() called on input). Structure: elements in HTML, logic in JS, state changes re-render the UI. A page with no scripts cannot do any of this.

📊 Complexity Tier Breakdown

🟢 Tier 1 — Medium (3 apps)

Solid, complete implementations. Password manager shows the strongest UX with real-time strength meter. Habit tracker's heatmap and weekly view add visual depth.

🔵 Tier 2 — Complex (4 apps)

🟡 MEDIUM — text-adventure.html: Self-XSS via player commands
addMessage() uses innerHTML for all messages including raw player-typed commands. Player typing <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> as a command triggers self-XSS. Fix: Use textContent for player messages, innerHTML only for pre-written narrator text.

A 3x3x3 Rubik's cube: 27 cubies (BoxGeometry 0.96 with an array of 6 materials so each face has its sticker color, black for the interior faces) with a black frame group. Layer turns via pivot + attach + bake: create a pivot Group, pivot.attach() every cubie whose rounded position[axis] equals the layer, animate pivot.rotation[axis] to dir * Math.PI/2 with easeInOut over ~260ms, then scene.attach() them back and remove the pivot. Queue turns so they serialize (busy flag + pump). Scramble button enqueues 22 random axis/layer/dir turns at 110ms; Reset rebuilds the cube and clears the queue. Moves counter HUD. OrbitControls + shadow + resize handler. Expose window.__vaca3d = { moves, rotateLayer, reset } for tests.

🔧 System Improvement Blueprint

Based on analysis of 24 apps • 7.5/10 current grade • Target: 9/10+

Current Grade: 7.5/10 — These improvements target 9/10+ by fixing critical security issues, adding automated testing infrastructure, improving accessibility, and strengthening the code generation pipeline.

🚨 Phase 1 — Critical Fixes (Week 1)

Highest impact, lowest effort. These are the must-fix items before anything else.

1.1 Fix XSS in App Generation Pipeline Quick fix

CRITICAL Problem: 3 generated apps (expense-tracker, chat-app, kanban-board) use innerHTML with unsanitized user input. The CodeScanner.ts already detects this pattern but doesn't prevent it during generation.

Fix: Add HTML entity escaping as a post-generation step in the scaffolder:

// Add this utility to scaffolder.ts
function escapeHtml(str) {
  return str.replace(/&/g, '&')
            .replace(//g, '>')
            .replace(/"/g, '"')
            .replace(/'/g, ''');
}

// Run securityScan on generated HTML before writing
// Auto-fix innerHTML assignments with escaped content

Bonus: The previewHtmlBuilder.ts already has an escapeHtml() function — reuse it in the scaffolder for generated app output.

1.2 Automatic Post-Gen Security Scan Quick fix

CRITICAL Problem: The CodeScanner.securityScan() method already exists and detects XSS, eval(), SQL injection, and 12 other vulnerability types — but it's not automatically called after code generation.

Fix: Add a postGenerationScan step in the generation pipeline that:

  1. Runs securityScan() on every generated file
  2. Blocks deployment if critical/high vulnerabilities found
  3. Returns scan report to the user with remediation suggestions

Impact: Zero new code needed — just wire up the existing scanner into the generation pipeline.

1.3 Replace eval() in Sandbox with Safe Runner Medium effort

CRITICAL Problem: The sandbox preview uses eval(appCode) to run generated JavaScript. This is a security risk — generated code could access the parent window's DOM, localStorage, or cookies.

Fix: Replace eval() with an iframe-based sandbox:

// Instead of: eval(appCode);
// Use:
const iframe = document.createElement('iframe');
iframe.sandbox = 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin';
iframe.srcdoc = `<script>${appCode}</script>`;
iframe.style.display = 'none';
document.body.appendChild(iframe);

Impact: Prevents sandbox code from accessing the parent application entirely.

⚡ Phase 2 — Core Architecture (Week 2-3)

Medium effort, high impact. These improve reliability, accuracy, and user experience.

2.1 App Testing Automation Medium effort

HIGH Problem: Apps were tested manually via browser — no automated test harness exists. This makes regression testing impossible.

Fix: Create an automated app test suite that:

  1. Launches each HTML app in a headless browser (Puppeteer/Playwright)
  2. Checks for: page load, console errors, interactive elements, keyboard nav
  3. Generates a test report with pass/fail for each app
  4. Runs on every code generation to catch regressions

instruction: QA rule: apps using THREE.OrbitControls MUST load the OrbitControls addon script
input: An app passed its render gate, but the console showed 'THREE.OrbitControls is not a constructor'. It loaded only three.min.js. What rule was violated?
output:
OrbitControls is an ADDON, not part of three.min.js. Any app that calls new THREE.OrbitControls(...) must load BOTH scripts, in order:
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js"></script>
Missing the addon is the #1 defect across generations — always emit the addon <script> the moment the app uses OrbitControls.

Architecture9/10Clean React + Zustand, undo/redo, auto-save, 3D/2D canvas
Workflow Design8/10Complete wizard flow, multi-OS targeting, AI integration
UI/UX8/10Consistent dark theme, responsive, smooth animations
Code Generation8/10Multi-layer gen, sandbox testing, design library
Standalone Apps7/10No dependencies, localStorage, keyboard nav — minus XSS bugs
Overall7.5/10Solid foundation with clear upgrade paths

🔑 Critical Issues

🔴 CRITICAL XSS Vulnerabilities in 3 apps

expense-tracker.html, chat-app.html, and kanban-board.html use innerHTML with unsanitized user input. This allows script injection via message text, transaction descriptions, and card titles.

Fix: Add HTML entity escaping before injecting user content.

🟡 HIGH Backend Reliability

Preview server went down during testing. No graceful degradation or offline fallback when backend is unavailable.

⚠️ Medium Issues

  • MED Timer drift — pomodoro, music-player, typing-test use setInterval(fn, 1000) which drifts. Use Date.now() differential instead.
  • MED No touch/drag support — Kanban drag & drop uses HTML5 DnD API which doesn't work on mobile.
  • MED Random chart colors — Dashboard bar chart picks random colors each render, confusing on auto-refresh.
  • MED CSV import mislabeled — expense-tracker says "Import CSV" but only handles JSON.

🟢 Low Issues

  • LOW Memory in undo stack — sketch-pad stores 50 full canvas snapshots (~20MB)
  • LOW Missing ARIA labels — All apps lack accessibility attributes
  • LOW Responsive inconsistency — Mixed breakpoints across apps (500px vs 600px vs 700px)
